analysis.title: 3Q Preview - What We're Watching For + Read-Throughs
key_insights: Mizuho reiterates Outperform and a $200 PT on SPCX (price $146.03) ahead of 3Q26 earnings. AI is the largest swing factor for 3Q26 revenue and EBITDA.

Consensus 3Q26 AI revenue is $6.30B (+146% Q/Q from $2.56B), split between AI Solutions & Infrastructure at $5.84B (from $2.19B) and Advertising at $658MM (from $367MM). Consensus AI adj. EBITDA is $3.32B (from $1.15B), a ~53% margin (from ~45%) and ~58% incremental margin.
Consensus consolidated 3Q26 revenue is $12.87B (+65% Q/Q), adj. EBITDA is $6.59B (+86% Q/Q) and adj. EPS is $0.15 (from ($0.09)). Consensus FY26 revenue is $44.6B (+139% Y/Y) and FY27 is $108.2B.

The key KPI is revenue per MW of compute. Consensus implies ~$15MM revenue/MW on AI Solutions & Infrastructure in 3Q26 versus ~$7MM in 2Q, roughly a doubling Q/Q and about 40% of the CoreWeave marker of ~$40MM/MW. Mizuho calls this a blunt calculation that uses nameplate rather than energized or utilized MW.

Nameplate compute was 1.4GW at the end of 2Q (1.0GW in 1Q, 400MW a year ago). Consensus is 1.74GW in 3Q26, 2.20GW in 4Q26 and ~5.8GW at YE27. The YE27 figure is at the low end of management's framing of capacity closer to 10GW than 5GW, which Mizuho flags as upside risk to consensus capacity.

CoreWeave disclosed signed 3-6 month contracts at ~$40MM/MW of annualized revenue. Nebius disclosed $20-25MM/MW/year on core 1-3 year agreements and $40-50MM/MW/year on shorter contracts. Mizuho would not apply these directly to SPCX because of duration and hardware differences.

SpaceX signed $14.1B of Cloud Services Agreements in 2Q and booked another $6.7B in the opening weeks of 3Q (~$20.8B combined), covering a six-month period that begins ramping in October. Mizuho says capacity, utilization and contracted $/MW are the constraints, not demand.

Capex math: consensus AI capex of $16.9B in 3Q26 and $18.7B in 4Q26 against +342MW and +457MW of nameplate adds implies ~$49MM and ~$41MM capex per incremental MW. A sub-one-year payback needs realized revenue/MW at or above capex/MW, well above the ~$15MM/MW consensus models and closer to the ~$40MM/MW marker.

Musk indicated ~780k GPUs deployed across Colossus 1 and 2, with ~220k GB300s expected near term, ~220k in November and potentially ~220k by late December. Mizuho estimates IT load could rise from ~1.4GW to ~1.8GW near term, ~2.3GW in November and ~2.7GW by late December, implying ~3.1GW of facility power at the meter by year-end. Mizuho finds progress versus plan encouraging.

Sensitivity: going from 1.74GW to 2.20GW adds ~460MW. That is ~$6.9B of annualized revenue at $15MM/MW, ~$11.5B at $25MM/MW and ~$18.4B at $40MM/MW. Each $10MM/MW of realized pricing is worth ~$4.6B of annualized revenue on that increment.
Consensus cash flow: operations $11.0B (from $2.4B), capex $19.6B (from $18.4B), free cash flow ($11.6B) (from ($15.95B)). Consensus 4Q26 FCF is ($10.3B).

Starlink consensus: subscribers 14.23MM (+2.23MM net adds vs 1.7MM in 2Q), ARPU $65.05 (from $66.00), Connectivity operating margin 38.3% (from 38.6%), Connectivity adj. EBITDA $2.94B (60% margin). Consensus has ARPU falling to $62.48 in 4Q26, so mix toward Enterprise/Gov't, Starshield and eventually mobile matters.

Space consensus: 1.9 Starship launches (from 1), 40.6 total launches (from 38), Space adj. EBITDA turning positive at $123MM (from ($205MM)) on revenue of $1.43B (+49% Q/Q). Mizuho says milestones (shorter intervals, booster recovery, ship reuse, commercial payload) matter more than cadence.

Network: consensus has 10,643 satellites in orbit (from ~10.2K). Mizuho wants V3 deployment commentary and network capacity as subs scale. Direct-to-cell matters less for 3Q numbers but is a potential TAM expansion.

Read-through for electrical and thermal names: consensus total capex steps from ~$67B in FY26 to ~$172B in FY27. Mizuho names VRT, ETN and HUBB (power distribution), JCI, TT and CARR (cooling) and PH (thermal and fluid handling) as most relevant, and ROK, EMR and AME for physical AI and automation.

Mizuho says consensus pricing assumptions remain too conservative into 2027 and that a sharp near-term pricing reset is hard to reconcile with current contracting, rising industry rates and capacity constraints.

Base-case PT of $200 is a 2029E sum-of-the-parts: Connectivity at 90% of plan ($43.6B EBITDA) at 15.0x, Space at 100% of plan ($3.1B) at 51.1x, AI at 90% of plan ($107.7B) at 16.8x, giving EV of ~$2,618B on 13.064B diluted shares. Bull case EV is ~$3,382B and bear case EV is ~$1,595B.

Risks: hyperscaler capex retrenchment, Starship slippage, xAI execution (plan requires ~225% revenue CAGR), governance (Musk holds 82.4% of votes), and lock-up supply (180-day tranche releases Dec 2026, Musk's 6.4B shares unlock June 2027).

market_movers.rationale: Mizuho keeps Outperform and a $200 PT ahead of 3Q26 results. It sees consensus compute pricing as too conservative into 2027, with ~$20.8B of contracted demand signed since 2Q began.
Mentioned as a read-through for neocloud pricing. CoreWeave signed 3-6 month contracts at ~$40MM/MW. The $88 PT is the latest in the rating history (10/15/26).

sector_views.sector: Industrials: electrical and thermal (data center exposed)
sector_views.rationale: SPCX's compute buildout is a visible demand signal for power and cooling content at VRT, ETN, HUBB, JCI, TT, CARR and PH. Mizuho will use the print and call to test its content-per-MW assumptions and order durability.

earnings_insights: SPCX 3Q26 consensus (not yet reported): revenue $12.87B (+65% Q/Q), adj. EBITDA $6.59B (+86% Q/Q), adj. EPS $0.15 versus ($0.09) in 2Q.
SPCX 3Q26 consensus AI revenue $6.30B (from $2.56B), AI adj. EBITDA $3.32B (from $1.15B), AI operating income ($14MM) (from ($1.26B)). All are consensus estimates, not reported figures.
SPCX consensus Starlink: 14.23MM subs, ARPU $65.05, Connectivity adj. EBITDA $2.94B at a 60% margin. These are consensus estimates ahead of the print.
SPCX consensus 3Q26 cash flow from operations $11.0B, capex $19.6B, FCF ($11.6B). Consensus FY26 revenue is $44.6B and FY27 is $108.2B.

Mizuho says a print near consensus on revenue with less capacity energized would mean a higher implied $/MW (supportive). A print on capacity but below consensus on revenue would point to pricing, duration or utilization pressure.
risk_factors: Hyperscaler capex retrenchment would deflate AI demand assumptions and compress xAI multiples across all scenarios.
Starship schedule slippage: each 12-month delay shifts Space EV and pushes out Terafab and orbital compute optionality.
xAI execution: the management plan requires ~225% revenue CAGR, and the bear/base gap on AI alone is $35B of EBITDA.
Governance: Musk holds 82.4% of the voting power and Class A minority holders have limited recourse.
Lock-up supply overhang: a 180-day tranche releases in Dec 2026 and Musk's 6.4B shares unlock in June 2027.
Execution risk on supply chain, power and political backlash for the compute buildout.
Multiple compression on AI from 16.8x to 13.5x drives the bulk of the bear case downside.
vol_and_positioning: Lock-up supply overhang: a 180-day tranche releases in Dec 2026 and Musk's 6.4B shares unlock in June 2027.
cross_bank_references: Mizuho references CoreWeave (covered by Gregg Moskowitz, Neutral) and Nebius contract pricing as markers for near-term AI capacity pricing.

tension_points.what_invalidates: A print on capacity (1.74GW) but below consensus revenue, which would point to pricing, duration or utilization pressure.
